detections.evidence_quote: Now, what was funny is I had some medical doctors telling me there's no such thing as leaky gut.
detections.summary: Researcher recounts his lab's history discovering and studying intestinal permeability ('leaky gut'), including pig and cell-culture experiments on ATP, oxygen and cytokine-driven barrier leakiness, and doctors' initial skepticism.

detections.evidence_quote: a repair enzyme inside the nucleus called PARP could get activated if your DNA is damaged
detections.summary: Speaker describes a Johns Hopkins group's work on neuro injury, explaining how a DNA-damage-activated enzyme called PARP depletes NAD and thus ATP.

detections.evidence_quote: there's all these articles by Harvard. Trained physicians on intestinal permeability.
detections.summary: Speaker cites articles by Harvard-trained physicians on intestinal permeability to counter doctors who denied leaky gut exists.

detections.evidence_quote: Solomon Snyder is one of the great neuroscientists of the 20th century
detections.summary: Speaker introduces the Johns Hopkins finding by emphasizing Solomon Snyder's stature as a great neuroscientist.
Speaker describes his lab's cell-based experiments showing ATP loss correlates with loss of gut barrier integrity, which were then published.

detections.evidence_quote: there's very little oxygen at the tip of the cells
detections.summary: Mechanistic explanation of low oxygen at the gut cell tips and ATP depletion associated with loss of gut barrier integrity.

verification_candidates.claim_text: Septic shock dramatically increases the leakiness of the gut.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: septic shock increases the leakiness of the gut quite dramatically
verification_candidates.rationale: Specific research finding, based on a pig model, about septic shock and gut permeability worth checking against later literature.

verification_candidates.claim_text: Exposing gut-lining cells to cytokines that mimic inflammation causes a large increase in barrier leakiness.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: we gave cytokines to these cells, mimicking inflammation. And sure enough, we had a big leak in in the monolayer.
verification_candidates.rationale: Cell-culture finding linking inflammatory cytokines to gut barrier leakiness; a specific mechanistic claim checkable against the literature.

verification_candidates.claim_text: A DNA-repair enzyme called PARP, when activated by DNA damage, depletes NAD, and without NAD the cell cannot make ATP.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: a repair enzyme inside the nucleus called PARP could get activated if your DNA is damaged
verification_candidates.rationale: Specific biochemical mechanism claim attributed to a Johns Hopkins research group, checkable against the literature.

verification_candidates.claim_text: Leaky gut (increased intestinal permeability) does not exist as a real physiological phenomenon.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: there's no such thing as leaky gut
verification_candidates.rationale: Central contested claim about whether leaky gut is real, framed as doctors' denial that the speaker rebuts with Harvard-physician articles; important to check against current medical consensus.
